doc.title: Jonathan Scales interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 23, 2025

title: How bandmates learn the parts
summary: He makes household-object demos and gives players written parts, chords and time signatures.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: How do your bandmates learn their parts? Do you do like demos for them or do they read the parts and then memorize?

It’s a combination of all that. So sometimes I’ll make like a demo in my own bastardized way. Like I would make these drum tracks sometimes where I would just like pick up random household objects and I’ll play the kick drum part on like a pillow and record it, like hitting the stick with a pillow or hitting the pillow with a stick, and I would make the hi-hat sound but like tapping on like a cup or something. And I would make these demos for the drummer to get the sense of you know, the style. And then, but I would put it all together so then you know the bass player would hear like this midi keyboard sound for like a bass idea, and they would hear the structure of the piece. But also they could see the time signatures, they can see the chords, they can see the melodies and the sections written out like on the page too.
